careerInfo: Andrew Kriegler has been President and Chief Executive Officer of the Investment Industry Regulatory Organization of Canada (IIROC) since late 2014.; Before coming to IIROC, Andrew served as Deputy Superintendent of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) where he was responsible for the prudential supervision of Canada's federally regulated financial institutions. He also spent 25 years in the private sector, most recently as Treasurer of CIBC from 2008 to 2012, and earlier as Senior Vice President & Chief Human Resources Officer of Moody's Corporation, parent of the credit rating agency Moody’s Investors Service, where he had been the Country Managing Director. ; Andrew has also worked as a treasury executive and as a securitization and debt capital markets banker and began his career as an analyst and then a trader on a mortgage-backed securities trading desk.
educationInfo: Andrew serves on the Board of Directors of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). He holds an MBA from the Ivey Business School at Western University and a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Economics from Trinity College in the University of Toronto.
summary: Andrew J. Kriegler is in the Executive Management Team and is the President and CEO

careerInfo: As General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Jennifer Armstrong is responsible for the legal and regulatory affairs of IIROC. This includes the administration of hearing panels, dealer and marketplace membership matters, and providing advice and support to the Board of Directors. Jennifer also oversees IIROC's communications mandate, which includes internal and external communications as well as the creation and delivery of member education services and investor resources.; Prior to joining IIROC, Jennifer served as Associate General Counsel and Managing Director at Bank of Montreal (BMO) Financial Group where she had oversight of BMO’s Canadian Capital Markets legal team and all activities relating to investment dealer activity including trading, equity research, investment banking, mergers and acquisitions and securities regulatory matters.; Before joining BMO, Jennifer spent 11 years in private practice at major Canadian law firms.
educationInfo: Jennifer holds an Honours Bachelor of Arts degree from Western University and a Bachelor of Laws degree from the University of Windsor.
summary: Jennifer Armstrong is in the Executive Management Team and is the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary

careerInfo: As Vice-President, Québec and Atlantic Canada, Claudyne Bienvenu directs IIROC's Compliance (Financial Operations, Business Conduct and Trading Conduct), Registration, Enforcement and Surveillance activities in Quebec and Atlantic Canada.; Before becoming Vice-President, Québec and Atlantic Canada, Claudyne served as Regional Director, Regulatory Affairs with IIROC and its predecessor organization, the Investment Dealers Association of Canada (IDA), which she joined in 2004.; Prior to joining the IDA, Claudyne worked in another regulatory role as a director in the Office of the President of Commission des valeurs mobilières du Québec, which itself is the predecessor of the Autorité des marchés financiers (Québec). In that role, she was responsible for relations with the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA).; Claudyne also served as an assessor on Québec's Human Rights Tribunal and as Québec representative in the Canadian Court Challenges Program.;
educationInfo: Claudyne received a Bachelor of Political Science from Laval University and a Bachelor of Laws degree from the University of Montreal in 1992. She has been a member of the Barreau du Québec since 1998.
summary: Claudyne Bienvenu is in the Executive Management Team and is the Vice-President, Québec and Atlantic Canada

careerInfo: As Chief Information Officer, Ian Campbell is responsible for leading the strategy, development and delivery of innovative, robust, and secure information technology solutions. Ian is also accountable for Information Security and the operational delivery of data sharing initiatives with and on behalf of our regulatory partners including public debt trade transparency.; Ian is a senior business and Information Technology leader with extensive experience in the broader financial and regulatory environments as well as in hi-tech industries.; Before joining IIROC, Ian served as Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer with the Canadian Securities Administrators. Ian also served in senior IT roles at Sun Life Financial and MTS Allstream, and acquired extensive global experience by working with Nortel Networks for more than a decade.; He holds a Masters degree in Business Administration and a Bachelor of Science, Business Administration and Computer Science from universities in Northern Ireland.;
summary: Ian Campbell is in the Executive Management Team and is the Chief Information Officer

careerInfo: Richard Korble manages IIROC operations in Western Canada. In that capacity, he directs Compliance (Financial Operations, Business Conduct and Trading Conduct), Registration, Enforcement and Surveillance activities.; Prior to joining IIROC in 2016, Richard was a partner and Chief Compliance Officer for a private equity dealer operating across Western Canada and Ontario.  Richard also has spent time with the Alberta Securities Commission, the Investment Industry Association of Canada and the Investment Dealers Association of Canada in regulatory and consultative activities.  His career began in retail banking and brokerage for a major Canadian Bank.  ;
educationInfo: He has a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Calgary and is CFA Charterholder.
summary: Richard Korble is in the Executive Management Team and is the Vice-President, Western Canada

careerInfo: As Chief Financial Officer, Laura McNeil is responsible for managing the organizations finances, including financial operations and planning, management of financial risks and cost recovery as a not-for-profit, and financial reporting to stakeholders, the Board of Directors and other members of the executive management team.; Laura joined IIROC in 2018 as Director, Finance Operations, was promoted to Vice-President, Finance in 2020, and appointed as Chief Financial Officer in 2021.; Before joining IIROC in 2018, Laura worked in Finance for Fortune 100/Fortune 500 broadly based healthcare companies, with progressive roles in financial planning and analysis, finance shared services and financial management. She also led an organizational change management team supporting a Canada-wide SAP deployment across five operating companies in three business sectors, six locations and more than a thousand users.
educationInfo: Laura holds an Honours Bachelor of Business Administration degree from Wilfrid Laurier University and is a Chartered Professional Accountant.
summary: Laura McNeil is in the Executive Management Team and is the Chief Financial Officer

careerInfo: As Senior Vice-President, Market Regulation, Victoria Pinnington is responsible for the management of all of IIROC's market-related activities, including policy development, audits, and oversight of Canadian debt and equity trading. She also oversees the development of IIROC's cross-product surveillance and analysis capabilities.; Victoria has been in the market regulation field for more than 20 years and has held a variety of positions at IIROC, most recently as Vice-President, Trading Review and Analysis responsible for the oversight of preliminary reviews of potential improper trading activity, post-trade surveillance, and market analytics.; Victoria is also the past Chair of the Intermarket Surveillance Group, an international group of exchanges, market centers, and market regulators that perform front-line market surveillance in their respective jurisdictions.; Before her career in market regulation, Victoria pursued a career in opera performance. She continues to perform regularly with the Canadian Opera Company.
summary: Victoria Pinnington is in the Executive Management Team and is the Senior Vice-President, Market Regulation

careerInfoDesignation: Senior Vice-President, Enforcement, Registration and Enterprise Risk
careerInfo: As Senior Vice-President, Enforcement, Registration and Enterprise Risk, Elsa Renzella oversees a variety of departments, which all play a critical role in IIROC's investor protection mandate. ; The Registration department ensures that individuals approved by IIROC satisfy certain suitability requirements including minimum proficiency and integrity standards.  IIROC's Enforcement department ensures Approved Persons and the investment dealers who employ them are appropriately disciplined when there is a violation of IIROC Rules.  Elsa also oversees the Complaints and Inquiries team, the primary contact for investor inquiries and complaints and works closely with Enforcement in identifying potential regulatory misconduct. Elsa is also responsible for IIROC's enterprise risk management and oversees its project management team. ; Elsa joined IIROC's predecessor organization, the Investment Dealers Association, in 2002 as Enforcement Counsel and later assumed the role of Director, Enforcement Litigation. In 2013, she became Vice-President, Enforcement, and was later appointed as Senior Vice President, Enforcement and Registration in January 2018, before taking on her current expanded responsibilities in 2021.
educationInfo: Elsa has extensive litigation experience, including work in private practice with a criminal defence law firm before starting her career in regulation. She holds a Bachelor of Business Administration degree from York University and a Bachelor of Laws degree from Osgoode Hall Law School.
summary: Elsa Renzella is in the Executive Management Team and is the Senior Vice-President, Enforcement, Registration and Enterprise Risk

careerInfoDesignation: Senior Vice-President, Member Regulation and Strategy
careerInfo: As Senior Vice-President, Member Regulation and Strategy, Irene Winel is responsible for the development and implementation of member regulation policy, as well as business conduct compliance and financial and operations compliance. She also leads the development of IIROC's organizational strategy, with the other members of IIROC's Executive Management Team.; Irene is a senior business leader, experienced in financial services operational management focusing on change and growth management, with expertise in legal, compliance and corporate governance.; Before joining IIROC, Irene served as Country Executive for Compliance and Operational Risk at Bank of America Merrill Lynch (BAML). Before joining BAML, Irene had been the Chief Compliance Officer with UBS Securities Canada and among other roles, Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer at HSBC Securities (Canada).; Irene previously served as a member of IIROC's Market Rules Advisory Committee and the Conduct, Compliance and Legal Advisory Section Executive. She has also served on the Ontario District Council.
educationInfo: A lawyer with a Juris Doctor from the University of Toronto and a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of British Columbia, Irene first worked in the industry as legal counsel at the Vancouver Stock Exchange after beginning her career in private practice in British Columbia.
summary: Irene Winel is in the Executive Management Team and is the Senior Vice-President, Member Regulation and Strategy

careerInfo: Paul D. Allison is the Chairman of Raymond James Ltd., overseeing the business building efforts and strategic leadership of the firm's Canadian operations including Equity Capital Markets, Private Client and Corporate Services. Mr. Allison also oversees Raymond James Financial Inc.'s Private Client business in the UK. Prior to joining the firm in August 2008, he worked as Executive Vice President and Vice-Chairman at Merrill Lynch Canada, as well as co-head of the firm's Investment Banking business. Before joining Merrill, he was head of Equity Capital Markets at BMO Nesbitt Burns, one of Canada’s leading bank-owned investment dealers.
educationInfo: Mr. Allison brings more than 35 years of senior capital markets and investment banking experience to this role including underwriting and arranging public and private debt and equity capital raising, as well as developing and managing retail products. An active volunteer in various charitable and industry organizations, is Board Chair of Drug Free Kids Canada, past Board Chair of the Humber River Hospital, member of the Humber River Hospital Foundation Campaign Cabinet; member of the Deans Business Advisory Council DeGroote School of Business McMaster University, and a former director of the Investment Industry Association of Canada.; Mr. Allison holds a Master of Business Administration degree (MBA) and a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering and Management from McMaster University. He is a member of the Association of Professional Engineers of British Columbia. Mr. Allison is Chair of IIROC’s Board and a member of IIROC’s Human Resources & Pension Committee.
summary: Paul D. Allison is one of the Board of Directors and is the Chairman, Raymond James Ltd.

careerInfoDesignation: President and Chief Executive Officer, Montréal Exchange (MX) and Global Head of Trading, TMX Group
careerInfo: Luc Fortin is President and Chief Executive Officer of the Montréal Exchange (MX) and Global Head of Trading, TMX Group. Luc’s key responsibilities include leading growth in TMX’s equities, derivatives, and fixed income trading businesses. In 2021, his mandate expanded to include oversight and strategic direction of CDCC and CDS, TMX’s post- trade businesses and crucial components of Canada’s capital markets infrastructure.; Luc joined MX as Managing Director, Derivatives Trading in June 2016, following a 25-year career in Canada’s capital markets industry leading client-facing teams in fixed income and derivatives. Prior to joining MX, he served as Managing Director, Canadian Head of the Institutional Client Group at HSBC Bank Canada.; In this role, Mr. Fortin led HSBC’s institutional client-facing businesses in rates and credit, derivatives, foreign exchange and money markets across Canada. Prior to HSBC, he held senior leadership positions at TD Bank and TD Securities.
educationInfo: Mr. Fortin is a graduate of the TD Securities Leadership program at Ivey Business School and holds a Bachelor of Commerce from University of Ottawa. He has served as Board Chair of CANMarket Data and was an Investment Industry Association of Canada board member from 2006-2010.
summary: Luc Fortin is one of the Board of Directors and is the President and Chief Executive Officer, Montréal Exchange (MX) and Global Head of Trading, TMX Group

careerInfoDesignation: Senior Vice‑President, Treasury Market and Liquidity Risk Management, CIBC
careerInfo: Tim Mills is the Senior Vice President, Treasury Market and Liquidity Risk Management at CIBC responsible for the risk management of the treasury, insurance and pension businesses. Previously at CIBC he was Vice President, Market Risk Management. Mr. Mills was a Senior Derivatives Trader at Kaupthing Singer & Friedlander, London, England. He was Head of Derivatives Trade at Nationwide Building Society in Northampton; Director, Private Fund Manager at Annex Capital Management, London; Associate Director, Equity Derivative Trading at UBS Warburg, London; Head of Fixed Income Trading – Asia at BMO Nesbit Burns/Bank of Montreal; and was a chartered accountant at KPMG Peat Marwick, London. ; Mr. Mills is a member of IIROC’s Finance, Audit & Risk Committee.
educationInfo: Mr. Mills has a Bachelor of Commerce and Finance (Honours) from the University of Toronto. He has a Certificate in Quantitative Finance, is a Chartered Financial Analyst and is a Chartered Accountant (FCA).
summary: Timothy Mills is one of the Board of Directors and is the Senior Vice‑President, Treasury Market and Liquidity Risk Management, CIBC

careerInfoDesignation: Executive Advisor to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the National Bank of Canada
careerInfo: Luc Paiement is Executive Advisor to the President and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bank of Canada. As Strategic Advisor, Mr. Paiement continues to actively contribute to the Bank’s success and development through his considerable experience.; Mr. Paiement joined Lévesque Beaubien in 1981 as an Investment Advisor and following the acquisition of Lévesque Beaubien in 1988 by National Bank of Canada, he has held several positions including Vice-President and Branch Manager; Senior Vice-President, Individual Investor Services; Executive Vice President, Corporate and Investment Banking; Executive Vice President Equity Capital Markets; President, Individual Investor Services; and Co-President and Co-Chief Executive Officer of National Bank Financial Inc. During the last 10 years, as Executive Vice President, he was head of the Wealth Management division of National Bank of Canada and as such, member of the Office of the President.; He has 39 years’ experience in the investment industry and is recognized for his strong interpersonal skills and his ability to focus on culture of customer service excellence. Mr. Paiement has been a key contributor to a series of transactions that have profoundly changed the organization.; Currently, he is on the Board of Directors of the Fondation Jean Lapointe and previously over the years, has been very active in raising funds for Festin de Babette, Fondation Docteur Maurice-Betrand, Moisson Montréal; Opération Enfant Soleil and UnitedWay/Centraide.
educationInfo: Mr. Paiement holds a Bachelor of Commerce degree from Concordia University in Montreal. He is also a member of IIROC’s Human Resources & Pension Committee.
summary: Luc Paiement is one of the Board of Directors and is the Executive Advisor to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the National Bank of Canada

careerInfoDesignation: Co-founder, Director, President & CEO, NEO Group of companies
careerInfo: Jos Schmitt is co-founder, Director, President & CEO of the NEO Group of companies, which includes the NEO Exchange - a Canadian stock exchange, and NEO Connect - a multi-asset distribution platform that enables the distribution of Platform Traded Funds (PTFs) as well as, in partnership with DealSquare, the distribution of private funds and private corporates. Prior to NEO and in the role of President & CEO, Mr. Schmitt formed the Alpha Group of companies, including the Alpha Stock Exchange. This followed his role as EVP Head of the Americas and Global Head of Capital Markets for Capco - a global professional services company focused on the financial services industry. During his tenure at this professional services company, where he was part of the original partnership group, he acted as strategic advisor and director of business and technology transformation programs for some of the largest stock and derivatives exchanges and clearing houses, alternative markets, data vendors and broker-dealers around the globe. Some of his other previous roles include President & CEO of a European derivatives exchange and clearing house; President & CEO of a pan-European indices publisher; Chairman of a derivatives SRO, and Head of Strategy and Business Operations at a European stock exchange.; Mr. Schmitt was actively involved with the Sunnybrook Hospital Foundation, where he was a Board member for 6 years, and is now a Board member of the Prosperity Project. He is also actively involved in advisory committees of the Ivey Business School and the Ecole des Sciences de la Gestion. He is a member of IIROC’s Human Resources & Pension Committee.
summary: Jos Schmitt is one of the Board of Directors and is the Co-founder, Director, President & CEO, NEO Group of companies

careerInfoDesignation: Corporate Director, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Quebecor inc. and Canada Infrastructure Bank
careerInfo: Michèle Colpron is a Corporate Director. She is currently a member of the Boards of Directors of Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Québecor inc. (including Québecor Média and Vidéotron Ltd) and Canada Infrastructure Bank. As a Corporate Director, she has developed expertise among others in Investments, Governance, Human Resources Audit and Risk committees.; Ms. Colpron has over 35 years’ experience in various strategic leadership roles within large organizations in the financial services industry in Canada, United Kingdom, Hong Kong and Switzerland. During her 12 years at Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec, Ms. Colpron was Senior Vice-President Financial Management from 2009 to 2012 ensuring sound management of the organization’s treasury activities including liquidity, leverage and coordinating financing activities on various bond markets. She was also responsible for the organization’s performance measurement for its portfolios and strategies.; As Vice-President Investment Administration from 2005 to 2009, Ms. Colpron was responsible for the liquid markets and private equity operations of the Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec. From 2000 to 2004 she was Vice-President, Finance and Administration for the private equity portfolios of the organization. In Switzerland from 1993 to 1999, Ms. Colpron held senior positions as Chief Financial Officer at Merrill Lynch Bank (Suisse) S.A. and Finance and Human Resources Manager of Standard Chartered Bank (Switzerland) S.A. Her foray into the international business began in 1989 with Ernst & Young in London followed by Hong Kong in 1991 until 1993 as audit manager.
educationInfo: Ms. Colpron is a Fellow of the Chartered Professional Accountant profession (FCPA, FCA) and she is also a qualified corporate director duly accredited by Laval University. She holds a Bachelor of Business Administration from HEC Montreal. Ms. Colpron is Chair of IIROC’s Human Resources and Pension Committee and a member of the Corporate Governance Committee.
summary: Michèle Colpron is one of the Board of Directors and is the Corporate Director, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Quebecor inc. and Canada Infrastructure Bank

description: Victoria Harnish is a retired public sector executive with extensive experience in organizational renewal, strategic and operational planning, revenue and expenditure planning and control, accountability systems, critical policy analysis and advice, policy implementation, and economic analysis. During her career with the Province of Nova Scotia, she served in several positions, including Public Service Commissioner, Secretary to Executive Council, Deputy Minister of Treasury and Policy Board and Deputy Minister of Finance. Ms. Harnish is currently Chair of the Halifax Dartmouth Bridge Commission and Chair of the Public Health Agency of Canada Departmental Audit Committee.  Past experience includes Chair, Statistics Canada Departmental Audit Committee, Member Health Canada Departmental Audit Committee,  and board member of Nova Scotia Health Authority;  Board of Governors of Mount Saint Vincent University; Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation; INNovaCorp; CoChair of the Nova Scotia Teachers Pension Partners Board; and Member of the Investment Advisory Committee for the Nova Scotia Teachers Pension Plan and the Nova Scotia Public Service Superannuation Plan. As a non-partisan Deputy Minister to several Nova Scotia Premiers and to Cabinet and its committees, she has a unique insight into political decision making and is very well positioned to address public policy and public interest considerations, government relations and communications strategy. Ms. Harnish has a Master of Public Administration (Management) from Dalhousie University and the ICD.D accreditation from the Institute of Corporate Directors. She is Chair of IIROC’s Corporate Governance Committee and a member of Finance, Audit & Risk Committee and Human Resources & Pension Committee.
summary: Victoria Harnish is one of the Board of Directors and is the Independent Director

careerInfoDesignation: Professor and TSE Chair in Capital Markets at the Faculty of Law, University of Toronto
careerInfo: Mr. Iacobucci is currently a member of the Board of Directors for the Empire Life Insurance Co. of Canada, and serves on the Audit Committee, Human Resources Committee and as Chair of the Conduct Review Committee. He was also previously a board member for ACS Media Income Fund, where he was Chair of the Compensation and Corporate Governance Committee, and the Dominion of Canada General Insurance Co., where he was Chair of the Conduct Review Committee.; Mr. Iacobucci is a member of IIROC’s Human Resources and Pension Committee.
educationInfo: Edward Iacobucci is Professor and TSE Chair in Capital Markets at the Faculty of Law, University of Toronto. He served as Dean of the Faculty from January 2015 to December 2020. His expertise relates to corporate governance, corporate finance, securities law and competition law. Since joining the Faculty of Law at the University of Toronto in 1998, he has been invited to visit University of Chicago Law School, Columbia Law School, NYU Law School, Tsinghua School of Law and the National University of Singapore Faculty of Law. He graduated from Queen’s University, Oxford University (which he attended as a Rhodes Scholar) and the Faculty of Law, University of Toronto.
summary: Edward Iacobucci is one of the Board of Directors and is the Professor and TSE Chair in Capital Markets at the Faculty of Law, University of Toronto

careerInfoDesignation: Chief Information Officer, Capital Region Housing Corporation (Edmonton)
careerInfo: Shenaz Jeraj is the Chief Information Officer at Civida (Edmonton) responsible for their technology and digital direction. Previously Ms. Jeraj worked at Dow Chemical, IBM and carried out a number of consulting engagements, including at the Alberta Health Services (AHS) on a multi-year project where she was the Integration and Change Management Leader. Ms. Jeraj has an extensive career as a technology and management consultant, strategy and change consultant and information management.; Ms. Jeraj is a member of IIROC’s Corporate Governance Committee and its Finance, Audit and Risk Committee.
educationInfo: Ms. Jeraj was a member of the University of Alberta’s Board Governors and continues as a member of the Audit and Risk Committee. Previously she was on the University Senate, Vice Chair of the Board, Chair of the Board Learning and Discoveries and member on the HR Compensation committee. Ms. Jeraj is a mentor at the Peter Lougheed Leadership College. Ms. Jeraj also served on the University Hospital Foundation, Board of Trustees, was a Judge for the Laurel Awards, a Sponsor and role model at WISEST, and served as President in Edmonton and then Vice President at Aga Khan Council for Canada.; Ms. Jeraj has a Bachelor of Science with a Specialization in Computing Science, from the University of Alberta. She received ICD.D certification from the Institute of Corporate Directors and is a Project Management Professional (PMP).
summary: Shenaz Jeraj is one of the Board of Directors and is the Chief Information Officer, Capital Region Housing Corporation (Edmonton)

description: Ms. Newman has extensive experience in finance, technology delivery, project & change management and data as well as running back-office operations. Most recently Ms. Newman spent more than 10 years at Canada’s largest single-profession pensions plan, the Ontario Teacher’s Pension Plan (OTPP). Prior to joining OTPP Ms. Newman worked at both CIBC and BMO holding various roles in Finance, Risk and Corporate Strategy.  She received her CPA (CA) while working at PWC in technology consulting and insolvency.  Ms. Newman brings extensive experience in financial operations, technology, risk and change management, through challenging times, in both the pension and banking sectors. Ms. Newman received the ICD.D designation from Rotman School of Business and the Institute of Corporate Directors, and a BCOMM (Hons) from Queen’s University.  Ms. Newman is IIROC’s vice-chair and is a member of the Corporate Governance Committee, and Chair of the Finance, Audit and Risk Committee.
summary: Jennifer Newman is one of the Board of Directors and is the Independent Director

careerInfoDesignation: Principal and Founder, Tralee Capital Markets Ltd.
careerInfo: Gerry O’Mahoney is the Principal and Founder of Tralee Capital Markets Ltd. through which he provides strategic and operational advice on all aspects of brokerage, investment management, wealth management, industry infrastructure and regulatory issues. He has extensive experience in the industry having served in various roles with TD Bank Financial Group. This includes ten years as Chief Operating Officer of TD Waterhouse Canada. Mr. O’Mahoney has served as the Chair of the IIROC Financial Administration Section (FAS) Operations Committee, as a member of the FAS Mutual Fund Dealer and Broker Committee, and in several committee roles with the Investment Funds Institute of Canada.; Mr. O’Mahoney served as a Director of CDS and was the Chair of the Canadian Capital Markets Association (CCMA). He has also served as a Director of World Vision Canada including 3 years as Chair of its Audit Committee; and was a member on its Executive Committee.
educationInfo: Mr. O’Mahoney has a B. Comm. from University College Dublin, Ireland, a graduate of the Manufacturing Executives Program from the University of Michigan and a C. Dir. from McMaster University’s Directors College. He is a member of IIROC’s Corporate Governance Committee and IIROC’s Finance, Audit and Risk Committee.
summary: Gerry J. O’Mahoney is one of the Board of Directors and is the Principal and Founder, Tralee Capital Markets Ltd.

description: Laura Tamblyn Watts is the CEO of CanAge, Canada’s national seniors’ advocacy organization. Her work focuses on aging, inclusion, consumer rights and social justice. She has previously served as Chief Public Policy Officer at the Canadian Association of Retired Persons and in a number of positions at the Canadian Centre for Elder Law including as their long-time National Director. She currently teaches Law and Aging at the University of Toronto where she is also a Fellow of the Institute for LifeCourse and Aging. Ms. Tamblyn Watts is past Board member of the Ombudsman for Banking Services and Investments (OBSI). Prior to joining OBSI’s Board, she Chaired OBSI’s Consumer and Investor Advisory Committee for 8 years. She is a Board member Elder Abuse Prevention Ontario, PACE Independent Living, and the NICE Network. Ms. Tamblyn Watts is a past Chair of the Canadian Bar Association’s National Elder Law section, where she sits as a current Executive member. She is a member of the Investment Funds Institute of Canada’s (IFIC) committee on Seniors and Vulnerable Investors (IFIC) and serves as a Canadian representative on the North American Securities Administrators Association (NASSA) Advisory committee on Vulnerable Investors. She is a continuing member of the Ontario Securities Commission’s Taskforce on Seniors. She helped to co-found Canada’s second low-income seniors’ legal services centre, SeniorsFirst BC, located in Vancouver, and served as its first Legal Director. She received her undergraduate honours degree in Political Science from Queen’s University and her law degree with honours from the University of Victoria. She was awarded the 2020/21 Community Leadership in Justice Fellowship by the Law Foundation of Ontario.  She was also awarded the Distinguished International Fellow Award from Stetson University Centre for Excellence in Elder Law and is a Canadian representative to the International Guardianship Network, and Fellow of the World Congress on Adult Guardianship. Ms. Tamblyn Watts is the author of numerous papers on aging issues, and is a frequent media commentator. She is a member of IIROC’s Corporate Governance Committee.
summary: Laura Tamblyn Watts is one of the Board of Directors and is the CEO, CanAge
